Title: Why Does AI Agent Security in Banking Require More Than Alerts?
Context: An agent can use legitimate credentials to create financial exposure without exploiting a vulnerability
Full Text:
TL;DR: AI agent security in banking requires controls that can deny prohibited workload actions before they complete, because an alert does not revoke an agent’s authority. An agent can use legitimate credentials to create financial exposure without exploiting a vulnerability. Aquasec combines deep runtime visibility with local enforcement through its full agent architecture, applying configured policies inside running workloads without waiting for centralized analysis. That control complements identity restrictions and transaction approvals, blocking supported operations that violate policy while the agent is executing.

What is the control gap in AI agent security?

Your bank’s exposure extends to the authority an agent’s workload gives it, which can be much broader than its assigned task. AI agent security must connect that task to enforceable limits on access and execution.

In Kubernetes, that authority can come from a service account, an associated cloud role, mounted credentials and available network paths. Instructions to inspect records do not remove credentials or close connections. A carefully written prompt therefore leaves the workload’s technical permissions unchanged. The agent can still attempt actions the business never intended it to take.

Why do internal AI agents require their own runtime controls?

Connecting an agent to production tools gives its decisions consequences inside your environment. A badly scoped instruction or a malicious prompt embedded in a document can lead it toward actions its existing access permits.

Blocking external agents at a customer login does nothing to constrain an internal agent using a workload identity. The bank still owns that exposure inside its clusters. Security cannot wait for a software exploit to establish that intervention is necessary, because an unwanted operation may use a valid credential and an allowed connection.

Where do access reviews and alerts fall short for AI agents?

Identity controls, image scanning and patching remain essential. They reduce unnecessary authority and address vulnerable software. A posture finding, however, leaves the identified access available until something changes it.

Adding runtime telemetry does not automatically close that gap. A sensor can observe an operation without being able to deny it locally. In a model that exports telemetry for centralized analysis and response, execution can continue while the decision is made.

For an agent connected to a financial system, that distinction is consequential. Investigating a completed operation and preventing that operation from completing produce different outcomes for the bank.

How should banks separate AI agent observation from action?

An agent assigned to inspect transactions should not automatically receive the authority to initiate them. Use dedicated identities and restrict available credentials to the resources its task requires. Require application approval for consequential operations, with read access limited to necessary records.

Then carry those boundaries into the running workload. Define the executable behavior and network destinations the task needs and enforce restrictions on supported operations outside that scope. The controls should hold when the agent misinterprets an instruction, without depending on the model to recognize its own mistake.

How does Aquasec enforce AI agent workload boundaries?

We put the enforcement decision inside the running workload through the Aquasec Enforcer. Our full agent architecture combines detailed runtime telemetry with local policy decisions at the kernel layer. In enforcement mode, it can deny supported operations that violate configured policy without waiting for centralized analysis or an analyst response.

Drift Prevention makes that distinction concrete. When an agent attempts to execute a binary introduced after deployment, the configured control can block execution. Network policies can also deny connections to prohibited destinations, restricting paths that the workload’s identity permissions might otherwise leave available.

Those controls act on the operation itself. Security teams get a way to constrain supported workload behavior while permissions are corrected, without making termination of the entire container the default response. Application authorization remains responsible for deciding which transactions an agent may perform.

The architectural distinction is whether the security component can apply the restriction inside the workload, without waiting for a separate response workflow.

How can an AI agent create financial exposure without an exploit?

Valid access can turn a poorly scoped task into an unintended transaction.

Example: A reconciliation agent is asked to resolve a failed settlement. Its workload holds a payment credential and can reach an internal transfer service. Without a separate approval check, it could attempt the settlement again from another funding account. Every step can use an allowed operation.

This hypothetical scenario explains the exposure; it is not a reported customer incident or a measured product result. The missing boundary is between the assigned task and the authority available to complete it.

What mistakes weaken AI agent workload controls?

Exceptions can reopen the access a runtime policy was intended to restrict. Do not approve broad exceptions just to remove a block. Validate the required dependency and limit the exception to what the application needs.

Do not treat a permitted connection as transaction approval. If read and transfer operations share the same allowed service, the application must authorize them separately. Workload network restrictions do not determine whether an individual financial transaction is legitimate.

What should banks demand from AI agent security next?

Banks should make demonstrated enforcement a condition of expanding AI agent access. Before giving an agent greater authority, require evidence that the controls protecting its workload can stop the prohibited behavior they are designed to address. An alert that leaves the operation untouched does not meet that standard.

We put that enforcement inside the running workload through the Aquasec Enforcer. That gives banks a way to restrict what an agent’s workload can execute, alongside the identity and application controls governing its access

FAQ

How does Aquasec differentiate AI agent security from runtime monitoring?

Aquasec combines runtime telemetry with local policy enforcement through a full agent architecture. For supported operations in enforcement mode, the workload does not need to wait for centralized analysis before a configured restriction can deny the action.

Can AI agent security stop misuse of valid credentials?

Aquasec can deny supported workload operations that violate configured policy even when credentials are available. A request that remains permitted still needs authorization and any required approval within the application.

Does this AI agent security strategy cover externally hosted agents?

Aquasec enforcement applies to supported workloads where it is deployed. Protecting a bank’s clusters does not automatically protect agents running on laptops or external platforms. Those deployments require their own access controls.

Title: Integrate Aquasec and Jenkins to Stop Unsafe Images Before They Run
Context: How does the Aquasec and Jenkins integration work
Full Text:
How does the Aquasec and Jenkins integration work?

The Aqua Security Scanner plugin is installed from the central Jenkins plugin repository, or deployed manually from its .hpi file. It is configured under Manage Jenkins, System, in the Aqua Security section. There an administrator sets the Aquasec scanner image, the Aquasec server URL and a scanner token. Both values come from the deployment command of a CI/CD scanner group. Aquasec SaaS accepts token authentication only, so username and password authentication is not an option for SaaS environments.

The plugin works in Pipeline and Freestyle jobs. In a pipeline, the aqua step goes into the pipeline script, and the Jenkins Snippet Generator can build the syntax. With the Docker engine, the plugin scans local images, images hosted in a registry and docker-archive tar files. With Podman, supported from plugin version 3.1.2, it scans local images as a root or non root user.

Each job chooses what happens to a noncompliant image: never fail the build, or perform the actions defined in the Image Assurance Policy. Local images and archives are evaluated against the Default Image Assurance Policy. Registry images are evaluated against every policy whose scope includes them. Optional settings register the image with Aquasec after a successful scan, hide base image vulnerabilities and run a shell command when an image fails.

Results appear in Jenkins as an Aquasec scan report organized like the image view in the Aquasec UI. A View in Aqua Platform button opens the image under Workload Protection, Images & Functions, Images, CI/CD Scans. A separate Aqua Security Serverless Scanner plugin scans function code for vulnerabilities, sensitive data and excessive permissions.

Title: Integrate Aquasec and Prometheus for Greater Visibility Into Runtime Security Operations
Context: Platform Aqua Platform Runtime Powered Cloud Security Monitor behavior, detect exploitable risk, enforce policy and contain threats across the application lifecycle
Full Text:
How does the Aquasec and Prometheus integration work?

The integration uses two separate configurations to make diagnostic metrics available to Prometheus.

Aquasec Platform monitoring

Administrators enable Prometheus under Administration, Integrations, Monitoring Systems in the Aquasec Platform.

The configuration supports an optional bearer token and a configurable data collection interval. Aquasec makes diagnostic metrics available at the specified interval, including the number of connected Enforcers and Gateways, images waiting to be scanned, images being scanned and images that failed scanning.

The integration also provides metrics for successful and failed user logins, defined Image Assurance Policies, Runtime Policies and Firewall Policies.

These metrics help teams understand the operational state of their Aquasec environment and identify patterns that may require attention.

Aquasec Enforcer monitoring

For more detailed runtime monitoring, Aquasec provides a Prometheus Metrics Exporter for Aquasec Enforcers and VM Enforcers.

Administrators enable the exporter under Settings, Enforcer, Prometheus Metrics Exporter. The exporter uses port 8995 by default, although this can be changed. The Metrics Exporter advanced setting must also be enabled for the relevant Enforcer groups.

The exporter exposes several categories of metrics, including:

Resource utilization: CPU and memory usage at the host and Enforcer levels, helping teams monitor the resources consumed by runtime protection.

Enforcer health: Enforcer version and type, active container counts, enabled functions and Gateway connection status.

Runtime security activity: File related events detected or blocked by runtime controls, malware scanning activity and behavioral detection event counts.

Security operations: Audit activity, event processing errors and host or image scanning results.

For Kubernetes deployments, Aquasec’s documentation provides an example using a local Prometheus server with service discovery to collect metrics within a cluster. A remote Prometheus server can use federation to collect metrics across clusters. Standalone Aquasec Enforcers and VM Enforcers do not require the local cluster deployment step.

This architecture allows organizations to monitor Aquasec metrics across distributed environments while maintaining the runtime enforcement capabilities that operate inside protected workloads.

Title: HTTP2Shell Vulnerability: How Should Security Teams Assess and Reduce Exposure?
Context: Aqua Team October 27, 2026 Updated: October 29th, 2026 TL;DR: The HTTP2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) is a critical flaw in Google’s Brotli decompression decoder that...
Full Text:
How is Aquasec addressing HTTP2Shell?

Aquasec has reviewed the impact of HTTP2Shell on its own components and confirmed that the affected Brotli library was present in certain Aquasec Enforcer images.

However, our security analysis determined that the vulnerable decoding functionality is not used by Enforcer components. The Enforcer does not decompress Brotli data, meaning the conditions required to exploit HTTP2Shell through the affected decoder are not present in the assessed Enforcer execution paths.

Our assessment included examination of both source code and released binaries to verify that the vulnerable decoder is not invoked during Enforcer operation.

Although the vulnerable library was not reachable through Enforcer functionality, we have released an updated Enforcer versions for both Update 47 and Update 45 LTS containing the corrected Brotli package.

Aquasec Enforcer 2022.4 U47 SP2 (2022.4.951.5) and 2022.4 U45 Enforcer LTS SP9 (2022.4.880.50) are now available. We recommend that customers upgrade to this release to remove the vulnerable dependency and address associated scanner findings.

Customers looking for additional information about affected versions, our technical assessment and upgrade guidance can refer to the Aquasec Support Knowledge Base and the U47 SP2 release documentation or the U45 Enforcer LTS SP9 release documentation

Title: PHP2Shell: How to Protect Vulnerable PHP Workloads While Patching
Context: Aquasec provides vulnerability detection and runtime controls to help identify exposure and restrict supported unauthorized activities while customers apply security updates
Full Text:
How does Aquasec protect PHP workloads?

Aquasec enforces security policies inside running workloads, allowing security teams to restrict supported unauthorized actions without depending exclusively on vulnerability specific signatures.

Four runtime control areas are particularly relevant to PHP workloads.

Restrict unauthorized process execution. Runtime policies can restrict PHP workloads from launching unnecessary shells and download utilities such as `sh`, `bash`, `curl` and `wget`. This can interrupt certain attempts to execute additional commands or retrieve malicious payloads.

Prevent unauthorized executable changes. Aquasec Drift Prevention can block execution of executable files that were not present in the original container image. This helps restrict newly introduced malicious binaries, although it does not independently prevent a PHP script from running through the existing interpreter.

Restrict unauthorized network activity. Appropriate runtime network controls can restrict unnecessary outbound connections and help limit certain reverse shell activities or communication with attacker controlled infrastructure.

Protect application files. File integrity monitoring can detect unauthorized modifications to sensitive application directories. File modification restrictions can prevent changes when properly configured, including changes to PHP web roots where malicious scripts might be introduced.

The effectiveness of these controls depends on workload coverage, policy configuration and the attack technique. In enforcement mode, validated policies can block supported unauthorized actions. They should not be represented as complete protection against either PHP2Shell vulnerability, particularly the reported memory disclosure path.

Title: How Do Financial Institutions Measure and Control Cyber Risk?
Context: Identify available policies that are not enforced, test relevant attack paths and document coverage and exceptions
Full Text:
What do financial regulations require institutions to demonstrate about cybersecurity controls?

Across five major regulatory regimes, financial institutions are expected to demonstrate effective management of technology risk and operational resilience. The requirements differ by jurisdiction, but they share an emphasis on accountable management, appropriate controls and evidence that those controls work.

United States: NYDFS Part 500 NYDFS Part 500 connects cybersecurity safeguards with executive accountability. For covered entities subject to the relevant provisions, annual submissions must be supported by evidence of material compliance or an acknowledgment identifying noncompliance and remediation. The regulation also addresses vulnerability management, access controls and tested incident response and recovery.

Runtime evidence can contribute to that record when it shows how an applicable control operated.

Canada: OSFI OSFI B-13 sets expectations for technology and cyber risk management, including control testing, asset inventories, preventive defenses and recovery.

E-21 connects that work to critical operations, dependencies, disruption tolerances and scenario testing. Full adherence was expected by September 1, 2026, with scenario testing for all critical operations to be completed by September 1, 2027. B-10 retains the institution’s accountability for third party arrangements.

A blocked container action becomes more useful when the institution can connect it to the critical operation it protects.

European Union: DORA DORA places ultimate responsibility for ICT risk with the management body. Its requirements cover ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and third party risk.

For financial entities subject to Article 24, appropriate tests must cover ICT systems and applications supporting critical or important functions at least annually. Control results should therefore inform remediation and the wider assessment of operational resilience.

Singapore: MAS MAS combines binding technology risk and cyber hygiene notices with supervisory guidance on technology risk, outsourcing and business continuity. For banks, the relevant notices are FSM-N05 and FSM-N06.

MAS emphasizes recoverable critical IT systems, customer information protection and critical business services with external dependencies.

A consultation on further technology risk management notice amendments ran from June 10 to July 31, 2026. Those proposals should be distinguished from requirements already in force.

Australia: APRA The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority places control effectiveness and operational resilience under board oversight.

CPS 234 requires information security controls proportionate to the information assets they protect, with systematic testing of effectiveness. CPS 230 connects operational risk to critical operations, disruption tolerances, tested continuity plans and oversight of material service providers.

For a payment service, runtime test results can help demonstrate which supporting workloads are protected, alongside evidence that the service can continue or recover within its tolerances.

How can Aquasec help?

Aquasec monitors the real behavior of running cloud native workloads, including process activity, network connections, file changes and privilege usage. That production context shows what an application is actually doing under operating conditions rather than relying only on what was known before deployment.

Observation is only the first step. Aquasec enforces policy locally at runtime, including blocking malicious execution, preventing privilege escalation and containing attacker activity. When an attack chain accelerates, local enforcement changes what the workload is allowed to do next without waiting for a separate analysis or approval workflow.

Aquasec Compass extends that operating model into agentic investigation, containment and remediation through the Model Context Protocol, with humans retaining control over consequential decisions. Attackers are using AI to reduce the time and labor inside their operations. Defenders need automation that reduces the time from evidence to bounded action.

Runtime protection does not replace patching, recovery planning or application layer security. It addresses the interval in which an active attack turns one malicious action into the next. In an AI accelerated ransomware operation, that interval is where containment can still change the outcome.
